answer: A refundable stake tied to a slowly earned reputation graph resists Sybil attacks: each identity must lock funds and gather endorsements from established peers before it can transact at full value. A whisper of trust from one peer means little, but a lantern of many independent attestations lights the way. Each fake vertex in the graph costs the same stake and waiting time as a real one, so a flood of sock puppets gains no cheap advantage — the attacker pays per identity while honest agents compound trust once.
